question.problem: What is the curvature of the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},{t}^{3}⟩$, for $t>0?$
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩=⟨2t,3{t}^{2}⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+(3{t}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+9{t}^{4}} \\  & =t\sqrt{4+9{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $t>0$, we have $|t|=t.$

Now, we find the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})⟩=⟨2,6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(t)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =⟨2t,\,3{t}^{2},\,0⟩\times ⟨2,\,6t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & 3{t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2 & 6t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 3{t}^{2} \\ 2 & 6t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =6{t}^{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the cross product is

$$
‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖=6{t}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{6{t}^{2}}{(t\sqrt{4+9{t}^{2}})^{3}} \\  & =\frac{6{t}^{2}}{{t}^{3}(4+9{t}^{2})^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{6}{t(4+9{t}^{2})^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
